title: Stochastic phase demultiplexer with tenant-aware latency budgeting
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Design and prototype a stochastic phase demultiplexer (SPD) that decides phase-splitting and admission at request time using probabilistic policies constrained by per-tenant latency budgets. Motivation: many current schedulers deterministically split prefill/decode phases and then apply coarse fairness heuristics; this leads to brittle tails for tenants with tight latency targets and to inefficient throughput utilization when kernels or attention patterns vary. The SPD will: 1) sample split decisions based on a learned/heuristic distribution that factors predicted kernel latency, attention sparsity, KV cache hit probability, and tenant budget headroom; 2) expose a compact tenant-level "latency budget" token (time/score) that the arbiter consumes to favor low-latency requests; 3) integrate with the kernel-latency estimator API (kernel-probe telemetry) to bias splits toward kernels with better short-sequence throughput when under tail pressure; 4) provide a safety fallback to deterministic splitting for sessions flagged as high-risk. Success metrics: p99 end-to-end decode latency delta per tenant (target <= +5ms for P1 tenants), tokens/sec throughput (no more than 6% regression at cluster level under realistic workloads), fairness measured by Jain's index across tenants on p95 latency, and energy/compute cost per token. Inputs/assumptions: we assume kernel-latency estimator endpoint (ENG-14207) provides current per-kernel microbenchmarks and that KV cache hit rate telemetry is available. We also assume per-tenant SLAs and budgets are surfaced in the tenant metadata service. Design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/cp/SPD-design-2026 (link placeholder). Prototype repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime-spd/tree/feat/stochastic-demux (PRs will be linked in comments). This ticket covers design, simulator, and a short lab rollout in the internal cluster; follow-on tickets will cover full rollout and telemetry plumbing.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Kickoff: scoped to design + discrete-event simulator. Initial design sketch posted to Confluence (SPD-design-2026). Assigned Diego for prototype and Priya for metrics dashboard.

2026-03-04 - Decision: use a hybrid approach — start with a rule-based sampler (heuristic weights) then collect data to train a light-weight online logistic model. Rationale: faster iteration and safer rollback compared to full RL approach.

2026-03-06 - Trade-offs noted: aggressive sampling reduces cluster throughput variability but increases scheduling jitter; will parameterize an "exploration cap" to bound impact. Also discussed potential interaction with quantization choices (see dependency ENG-82314).

2026-03-08 - Prototype: simulator emits sample traces showing 12% reduction in p99 for latency-sensitive tenant when sampling split probability tuned to kernel-latency signal; cluster throughput regression in simulator ~3.5%. Saved simulation artifacts to drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/SPD-sims-2026 (placeholder).

2026-03-10 - Ready for design review: attached detailed flow diagram, API sketch for tenant budget token, and canary plan. Reviewers requested explicit rollback criteria and hazard checks for KV-cache-thrashing; added to follow-up tasks.
